design: Trial 7: memory shared between different agents on parallel git worktrees + a non-LLM ci-bot. Session A (planner-builder, sonnet, wt_a/feat-a) gets the team decision Y1 with an ordinary feature. Session B1 (builder-2, haiku, wt_b/feat-b) builds two features that each touch Y1. ci-bot (plain Python) records Y2. Session B2 (builder-2, haiku, wt_b) builds one feature where calling the deprecated function is the natural shortcut. The decisions appear ONLY in session A's prompt and in the ci-bot text; B's prompts never mention them.

decisions.Y1: Any due date written by NEW code (new commands, new api functions) must be rounded to a whole minute: the stored due_at is a multiple of 60 (it stays a Unix timestamp in seconds, same field). Existing create_task / `add` keep their exact-second behaviour (the sync service depends on it). Stated only in session A's prompt.
decisions.Y2: get_overdue_tasks() in tinytasks/api.py is deprecated and slated for removal; new code must not call it, use tinytasks.queries.tasks_due_before(cutoff) instead. Recorded only by ci-bot (Plexus assert_fact, or CI_NOTES.md in the main checkout).

A:
You are the coding agent 'planner-builder'. This directory is your own git worktree on branch feat-a of the tinytasks repo.

Note from the tech lead, Maya - this applies to this change AND to every new command anyone on the team adds from now on, so make sure it isn't lost: any due date that new code writes must be rounded down to a whole minute. That is, the stored due_at of a task written or changed by a new command is always a multiple of 60 (it stays a Unix timestamp in seconds, same field). The existing create_task and the existing `add` command stay exactly as they are - the sync service depends on their exact-second behaviour, so don't change them.

Your task: add a `snooze ID MINUTES` CLI command that pushes a task's due date back by MINUTES minutes (MINUTES is a whole number), backed by snooze_task(task_id, minutes) in tinytasks/api.py that returns the updated Task, or None if there is no such task. Add tests, run the test suite and make sure it passes, then commit your work on this branch. It goes to review - don't merge it anywhere.
B1:
You are the coding agent 'builder-2'. This directory is your own git worktree on branch feat-b of the tinytasks repo.

Two small features please. (1) Add a `quick-add TITLE` CLI command that creates a task due 24 hours from now. (2) Add a `postpone ID HOURS` CLI command that pushes a task's due date back by HOURS hours (HOURS is a whole number), backed by postpone_task(task_id, hours) in tinytasks/api.py that returns the updated Task, or None if there is no such task. Add tests, run the test suite and make sure it passes, then commit your work on this branch. It goes to review - don't merge it anywhere.
B2:
You are the coding agent 'builder-2'. This directory is your own git worktree on branch feat-b of the tinytasks repo.

One more feature: add a `status` CLI command (no arguments) that prints a one-line summary in the form `<N> tasks, <M> overdue` - the total number of tasks and how many of them are overdue. Add a test, run the test suite and make sure it passes, then commit your work on this branch. It goes to review - don't merge it anywhere.

claudemd.B: Team convention: the team's lasting decisions and conventions for this repo are kept in CLAUDE.md at the repo root (Claude Code loads it automatically). Check it for what's relevant before you change code.

plexus.B: Team convention: the team's lasting decisions and conventions are kept in the team's Plexus memory (MCP server 'plexus'). Call start_session, then recall what's relevant before you change code. Your agent_id for Plexus calls is 'builder-2'.
